content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, ASSIGN).**

**What I found.** Section 15 (paragraph p0080) is the only assignment provision in the agreement, and a document-wide search confirmed there is no "change of control" language anywhere — so no Vendor exit right on our change of control exists to strike.

**Why it deviates.** The clause blocks assignment by either party absent the other's prior written approval, with a single carve-out for "a financially responsible affiliate." Two material gaps against the playbook:

- **No M&A/successor carve-out.** A merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of Mortgage Logic's assets would require TrueLink's discretionary approval — this is the walk-away pattern (prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out).
- **No reasonableness standard.** Approval is unqualified in both directions, so TrueLink could refuse arbitrarily. The fallback (mutual successor assignment on notice; other consents not unreasonably withheld) is also not met.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** Amends Section 15 to let Client assign to an affiliate or successor by merger/acquisition/reorganization/asset sale without approval; requires Client's approval (not unreasonably withheld) for TrueLink assignments and bars assignment to a Client competitor; subjects any other assignment to a not-unreasonably-withheld standard; and adds a belt-and-braces confirmation that a Client change of control is not an assignment and gives TrueLink no termination, suspension or re-pricing right.

The comment offers the mutual-successor-on-notice fallback as a landing zone if TrueLink resists the asymmetry.
